claim: A standalone Netdata Agent has a measured footprint of 1-5% of a single CPU core with default settings (up to 5-20% in production) and 100-200 MB RAM on an empty system (250-350 MB in typical production), with ~4 GiB disk by default (3 GiB metrics plus metadata).
stance_target: Benchmark for the resource budget a jupiterOS fleet agent must beat or match
scope_conditions: Official vendor documentation, Netdata Agent current version, default settings, Linux; dbengine mode, 3 tiers
quoted_support: CPU 1%-5% of a single core with default settings; up to 5%-20% in production. RAM 100-200 MB on an empty system; 250-350 MB in typical production. Disk ~4 GiB by default (3 GiB metrics plus metadata), configurable per tier.

claim: Netdata's recommended fleet architecture is Parent-Child streaming: lightweight Child agents on production/edge hosts (optionally db mode = ram to eliminate child disk I/O) stream metrics to Parent nodes that centralise dbengine tiers, retention, ML, and health alerting.
stance_target: Centralised-store vs edge-light agent architecture for jupiterOS fleet monitoring
scope_conditions: Vendor best practice; multi-node Netdata deployments
quoted_support: In a Parent-Child setup, switch the Child's database mode to ram. This eliminates disk I/O for the Child. ... centralizing the collection and processing of metrics on Parent nodes while running lightweight Children Agents on edge devices.

claim: Netdata collects most metrics at 1-second granularity by default, and lowering the sampling frequency from 1s to 2s intervals can approximately halve CPU usage.
stance_target: Sampling-interval tradeoff for a lightweight Rust fleet agent
quoted_support: Netdata collects most metrics with 1-second granularity. This high frequency impacts CPU usage. ... Lowering the sampling frequency (e.g., 1-second to 2-second intervals) can halve CPU usage.

claim: Netdata's storage engine stores time-series in a custom 32-bit floating-point format with an anomaly bit, using a fixed-step database design and pointer-referenced label storage to minimise memory and disk usage.
stance_target: Design techniques a lean agent can borrow for metric storage efficiency
scope_conditions: dbengine storage engine internals, vendor description
quoted_support: Netdata uses a custom 32-bit floating-point format tailored for efficient storage of time-series data, along with an anomaly bit. This, combined with a fixed-step database design, enables efficient storage and retrieval of data.
